title: Johnny Dodds, Jimmy Noone and old clarinetists
summary: Dodds took over from Duhé with Kid Ory; Jimmy Noone, Bechet, Tio and McCurdy are discussed.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Well, that tape is just about around the corner. Yeah, I guess. Any other questions you'd like to...
No, I was thinking if Lawrence knew Johnny Dodds. Oh, for sure. Oh yeah. Johnny is one of my favorite clarinet singers. Oh yeah?

Yeah. Well, I... Johnny Dodd took over after I left Kid Ory. That's who I used to be. Yeah. Yeah, he started with Kid Ory after. I left Kid Ory. And Jimmy Noon, I guess you knew him. Oh yeah, he... He was playing one cabaret, I was playing the other when he went up to country. Another good Tony's clarinet.

Yeah, he used to get around very fast on the clarinet. Yeah. Did the old time fellas though, like the T.O's and Warner and some of those, get all over the clarinet and the clarinet up high and low and... Oh, I don't know. Run all over the clarinet.

Oh yeah, Bach-Ate, Bach-Ate, T.O. Oh yeah, that's bad. With all the arpeggios and the chords, they didn't just stick to the melody of them. Oh, no, no, they didn't run up that scale. Somebody told me maybe they... Diminished, diminished with them. Yeah, all the different... Variations, kind of variation. Oh, it's really bad clarinet, Bach-Ate, T.O.
Oh, he is a good one too, with the rubber shorts. He was a good one too. He was a good one. Charlie McCurdy, yeah.
